children: Emkay Global Financial' research report on Bank of Baroda

BoB reported a sharp ~25% PAT beat at Rs65bn (ROA of ~1.3%), led by higher other income from NSE stake sale gains (Rs13bn) and investment revaluation. Advances grew 18.5% yoy, led by the RAM segment and overseas portfolio (aided by FCNR(B) leverage), while ex-FCNR(B) growth stood at 13.5%. Deposits grew 16.4% yoy, aided by FCNR(B) mobilization of Rs1,026bn, which is being maintained as stored liquidity and can be deployed in coming quarters. NIM moderated to 2.74%, with the management retaining FY27 guidance of 2.75–2.95%. Asset quality improved qoq, with the bank building prudential buffers through additional provisions of Rs16bn (Rs13bn toward specific NPAs and Rs3bn toward investment valuation risks), while remaining cautious on gold loan growth. The bank raised FY27 credit growth guidance to 13–15% (from 12–14%) and deposit growth guidance to 11–13% (from 10–12%) and expects ROA to remain ~1% for FY27. We fine-tune our earnings estimates and expect BoB to deliver a healthy ~1% ROA over FY27-29E.
Thus, we retain BUY and TP of Rs300, valuing the standalone bank at 0.8x Sep-28E ABV and subsidiaries/investments at Rs15/share.
